items.title: A client reports sudden tearing chest pain radiating to the back. BP is 204/110 mm Hg in the right arm and 172/96 mm Hg in the left. What is the priority action?
items.content: Activate emergency evaluation and prepare for rapid blood pressure and heart-rate control as prescribed.
items.rationale: Abrupt tearing pain and unequal arm pressures suggest aortic dissection. This is a vascular emergency requiring urgent imaging and controlled reduction of shear stress.

items.title: A client receiving peritoneal dialysis reports abdominal pain and cloudy effluent. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
items.content: Notify the dialysis team promptly; collect effluent for cell count and culture as prescribed; assess temperature and abdominal findings; administer prescribed intraperitoneal antimicrobials.
items.rationale: Cloudy dialysate and abdominal pain suggest peritonitis. Prompt specimen collection and antimicrobial treatment are important to preserve peritoneal function and prevent sepsis.

items.title: A client has dysphagia after a stroke. Select the 3 actions that reduce aspiration risk during oral intake.
items.content: Keep the client upright at 90 degrees; follow the prescribed texture and liquid consistency; check for pocketing and maintain upright positioning after meals.
items.rationale: Upright posture, prescribed consistency, and checking for retained food reduce aspiration. Oral intake should begin only after an appropriate swallow assessment.

items.title: Match each finding with the more likely vascular disorder.
items.content: rows:leg pain with walking relieved by rest;brown ankle discoloration with edema;cool foot with diminished pulses|columns:peripheral arterial disease;chronic venous insufficiency|answers:leg pain with walking relieved by rest=peripheral arterial disease;brown ankle discoloration with edema=chronic venous insufficiency;cool foot with diminished pulses=peripheral arterial disease
items.rationale: Intermittent claudication, coolness, and diminished pulses suggest arterial insufficiency. Dependent edema and brown gaiter-area pigmentation are characteristic of chronic venous disease.

items.title: A client with untreated hyperthyroidism has fever 40 °C, severe tachycardia, agitation, and vomiting. Suspect ___. Priority supportive care includes cooling and prescribed ___; monitor for ___ instability.
items.content: thyroid storm|beta blocker and antithyroid therapy|cardiovascular
items.rationale: Thyroid storm is life-threatening thyrotoxicosis. Treatment includes supportive cooling, beta blockade, antithyroid medication, and close cardiovascular monitoring.

items.title: A client with cirrhosis vomits a large amount of bright-red blood and becomes hypotensive and tachycardic. Select the likely condition, two actions, and two parameters to monitor.
items.content: condition:acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage|actions:establish large-bore IV access and initiate prescribed resuscitation;prepare for urgent endoscopy and prescribed vasoactive therapy if variceal bleeding is suspected|monitor:hemodynamic status;hemoglobin and ongoing blood loss
items.rationale: Hematemesis with shock in cirrhosis suggests major upper GI bleeding, potentially variceal. Resuscitation and urgent definitive evaluation are required; monitor perfusion and blood loss.

items.title: Highlight findings in a febrile client that suggest meningococcemia and require immediate escalation: rapidly spreading nonblanching petechiae; severe headache and neck stiffness; mild seasonal sneezing; hypotension; cool mottled extremities.
items.content: segments:rapidly spreading nonblanching petechiae|severe headache and neck stiffness|mild seasonal sneezing|hypotension|cool mottled extremities|correct:1,2,4,5
items.rationale: A rapidly spreading purpuric rash, meningismus, hypotension, and poor perfusion can indicate meningococcal sepsis. Immediate isolation, antimicrobials, and resuscitation are essential.

items.title: The prescription is 750 mg. The available tablets contain 250 mg each. How many tablets should the nurse administer?
items.rationale: 750 mg ÷ 250 mg per tablet = 3 tablets. Verify the formulation and whether the prescribed dose is within the safe range.

items.title: A client taking digoxin has potassium values of 4.1, 3.4, and 2.8 mEq/L over 24 hours and develops nausea and a pulse of 50/min. What is the priority interpretation?
items.content: The client is at increased risk for digoxin toxicity and dysrhythmia; withhold the dose and escalate for urgent evaluation.
items.rationale: Falling potassium increases myocardial sensitivity to digoxin. New nausea and bradycardia are concerning for toxicity and require withholding the dose, ECG assessment, and urgent review.
